key_numbers.metric: GPT-4.0 vs GPT-3.5 accuracy delta

structure_gain: none reported (no ablation isolates the dangerous-flow/slicing representation itself against raw decompiled code on the same model)
confound_note: Central comparison against Emtaint/Arbiter/Karonte varies tool architecture, internal representation, and often binary form (stripped vs symbol-table) together; the one clean ablation (Table 3) varies model (GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5), not representation.
stop_detail: Backward interprocedural data-dependency slicing from taint sources to vulnerable sinks builds 'dangerous flow' call chains (Def 4.2, Sec 5) that ground the LLM's step-by-step function-by-function analysis via sequential prompt templates (Sec 5.3).
threats_to_datum: LLM output instability under temperature noted as a limitation (Sec 6.2.1); source/sink identification precision is imperfect (~82% avg, Table 4); no explicit check for training-data contamination on Juliet, though Karonte firmware was confirmed unseen.

key_numbers.metric: F1 on BigVul (vs best baseline LineVul+DeepDFA)
F1 on PreciseBugs (post-cutoff, unseen) vs LineVul
GNN-embedding ablation on BigVul (MSIVD- vs MSIVD)

structure_gain: Adding CFG/DFA-derived GGNN embeddings to the fine-tuned LLM's hidden states raises F1 from 0.90 (LLM-only, MSIVD-) to 0.92 (MSIVD) on BigVul, holding the CodeLlama-13B backbone and training budget fixed (Table 4).
confound_note: The GNN-presence ablation (Table 4) cleanly holds model/budget fixed and varies only representation; but the headline BigVul-vs-baselines and BigVul-vs-PreciseBugs comparisons vary model, training data, and dataset simultaneously, and PreciseBugs evaluation drops the GNN component entirely.
stop_detail: Reaching-definition dataflow analysis computed over each function's CFG is embedded via a GGNN and concatenated to the LLM's final hidden states before classification (Section 3.3).
threats_to_datum: Likely LLM memorization of BigVul is only partly mitigated via the temporally-filtered PreciseBugs set; BigVul itself has known label noise/selection bias from bug-fix-commit mining; the GNN was tuned specifically for BigVul's CFGs so the PreciseBugs generalization test omits it (Section 6).

demote_reason: Full text confirms EnStack simply fine-tunes and ensembles standard pretrained code-LMs (CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, UniXcoder) via stacking meta-classifiers on their output probability vectors; no novel program representation or context-construction mechanism is introduced or studied. GraphCodeBERT's built-in DFG handling is used off-the-shelf and is never isolated or varied -- the only ablation (Fig. 4) varies model combination and meta-classifier choice, not representation.

key_numbers.metric: F1, DeepSeek-R1+CoT: API-abstraction level A3 vs w/o-API context
F1 vs best context-sampling baseline (API-guided sampling)
CodeLLaMA+BP F1 vs best baseline (hierarchy sampling, HS-C)

structure_gain: API-abstraction context (level A3) raises F1 from 60.19% (w/o-API context) to 69.09% on DeepSeek-R1+CoT, same model and prompting strategy, only representation varied (Table 4, Sec 5.1.1).
confound_note: The primary ablation (w/o-API vs A1-A4) holds model and code content fixed and varies only context abstraction level -- a clean representation-only comparison; the baseline comparison against All-Callees/Random/Hierarchy sampling additionally varies prompting strategy across models, so representation is not perfectly isolated there.
stop_detail: Control-flow and data-flow analysis over the target function and its callees (up to 3 call layers) extracts four API-usage features (fuzzy/concrete branches, call counts, key variables) at four increasing abstraction levels A1-A4, appended directly into the LLM prompt (Section 3.2.2, 3.3.1).
threats_to_datum: Static alias-analysis imprecision degrades the most abstract level (A4); DeepSeek-V3 shows high run-to-run performance volatility; evaluation limited to 623 historical CVE samples with no cross-project or production validation (Sections 5.1.3, 5.3.1, 6.2).

venue: Internetware 2025 (16th Asia-Pacific Symposium on Internetware), ACM ICPS, New Idea track
demote_reason: Full text shows only qualitative validation on four real-world attack incidents (Table 5), each checked by whether the LLM's narrative output named the correct known attack type; no precision, recall, F1, detection rate, or any other quantitative detection metric is reported anywhere in the paper (Section 4.1).

key_numbers.metric: fix accuracy, fine-tuned SecureFixAgent
false positive rate
gains vs baselines (abstract)
key_numbers.value: +13.51pp fix accuracy vs pre-trained LLMs; -10.8pp FP vs static analysis alone; -5.46pp FP vs pre-trained LLMs

structure_gain: No representation-only ablation; reported gain is from the iterative validate-loop vs single-pass LLM: fix accuracy rises from 79.72% (LLM-only, converges at iteration 1) to 87.83% (SecureFixAgent, converges at iteration 3) (Fig. 2, Table III).
confound_note: Central comparison (SecureFixAgent vs Bandit-only vs single-pass LLM) varies presence of the iterative detect-repair-validate agent loop and fine-tuning together, not representation alone; the code+Bandit-report input format is held constant across arms.
stop_detail: Bandit static-analysis findings (vulnerable segment, rule report) plus full source are fed to the LLM each iteration, and each proposed patch is re-validated by re-running Bandit until convergence or the iteration limit (Algorithm 1, Sec III-B/III-E).
threats_to_datum: Detection scope is bounded by Bandit's rule set; multi-file/distributed-logic patches often remain incomplete after the iteration cap; developer study is small (n=15) and Likert-based; no comparison to commercial tools like Copilot/Semgrep (Section VI-B).

key_numbers.metric: F1 (SFT+DPO) on FORGE
F1 progression Base -> SFT -> SFT+DPO
avg detection time per contract vs baselines

structure_gain: none reported for representation directly (the knowledge-graph structure is held constant); reported gains are from fine-tuning stages: F1 rises Base 57.8% -> SFT 65.5% -> SFT+DPO 74.9% (Table 1), not a raw-text-vs-KG ablation.
confound_note: The Base/SFT/SFT+DPO comparison holds the knowledge-graph representation fixed and varies only the model training regime; the comparison against Achecker/GPTScan baselines (Table 2) varies representation and tool architecture together, not representation alone.
stop_detail: Slither's IR is traversed to build a two-layer (ontology+instance) contract knowledge graph capturing control-flow, invocation, and inheritance relations (Sec 3.1); the SFT+DPO-tuned LLM translates NL vulnerability patterns into SPARQL queries executed against this graph to ground detections (Sec 3.2).
threats_to_datum: Authors note the KG is built from static AST/IR extraction and may yield 'shallow semantic representations' for complex cases; evaluation is restricted to one dataset (FORGE) and one CWE family (access control), with unclear transfer to other LLM backbones (Section 1, 5).

key_numbers.value: up to 225M input / 38M output tokens, ~448 min/project average

structure_gain: No controlled representation ablation; qualitative contrast: IRIS's systematic API enumeration reaches 46.15% recall on CWE-078 vs LLMDFA's LLM-inferred sources/sinks at 0% on the same CWE (Section V-A) -- but model, workflow, and representation all differ simultaneously.
confound_note: Compares five published tools 'as-is' (RepoAudit, KNighter, IRIS, LLMDFA, INFERROI): LLM backbone, source/sink specification method, workflow architecture, and representation (CFG/CPG/call-graph/CodeQL-template) all vary simultaneously across arms; not a controlled ablation.
stop_detail: Different tools ground detections differently -- e.g., INFERROI explores paths over the CFG, RepoAudit performs 3-layer interprocedural callee/caller exploration to bound path explosion, IRIS embeds LLM inferences into CodeQL query templates (Introduction, Section V).
threats_to_datum: False-positive labeling by two authors (>150 human hours) with double-coding to reduce subjectivity, but classification may still reflect labeler interpretation; study limited to C/C++ and Java, 5 LLM tools + 2 traditional tools, so findings 'may not generalize uniformly' to other languages or newer models (Section VI-B).

key_numbers.metric: overall valid-exploit confirmation rate vs best baseline (Explode.js Pkg mode)
private NodeMedic dataset valid PoC rate vs NodeMedic-FINE
newly crawled npm packages (Wild): validated vulnerabilities found

structure_gain: Paper argues a representation-light agent (raw source + lightweight tooling, no dedicated static/dynamic taint engine) outperforms CPG/taint-provenance-graph-based tools (83.75% vs 43.13% confirmation rate, Table 3) and an LLM+program-analysis hybrid, PoCGen, at lower cost (Table 4) -- i.e. less built-in structure yields better results here, the opposite direction from most representation-gain findings.
confound_note: Central comparison (LLMVD.js vs FAST/NodeMedic-FINE/Explode.js/PoCGen) varies representation (raw-code+agent-search vs CPG/taint-provenance-graph/CodeQL-derived structure), LLM backbone use, and tool architecture simultaneously -- not an isolated representation ablation on one fixed model.
stop_detail: A ReAct-style multi-agent pipeline (Finder -> Judge -> Constraints Inferencer -> Exploiter) reasons over raw source retrieved via pattern-based file search, then grounds each finding via oracle-guided PoC execution that checks concrete side effects rather than relying on model self-report (Sections 4.3-4.4).
threats_to_datum: Public benchmarks predate the LLM's training cutoff and memorization is only partly mitigated by a code-transformed variant; the NodeMedic dataset has distribution bias (only NodeMedic-FINE-flagged packages); evaluation is restricted to 4 taint-style vulnerability classes, limiting generalizability (Section 6, Threats to Validity).

key_numbers.metric: pairwise accuracy, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (reproduction vs original)
performance plateau across all evaluated open-weight models

structure_gain: none reported -- the RAG knowledge-base/retrieval representation is held fixed (reused from the original Vul-RAG) across all comparisons; gains/losses are attributed to model family, scale, and reasoning capability, not to representation variation.
confound_note: All RQs vary the underlying LLM (family, code-specialization, reasoning ability, parameter scale 3B-32B) while holding the Vul-RAG retrieval pipeline and knowledge base fixed -- the inverse of a representation ablation, so representation's own contribution is not isolated from base LLM capability.
stop_detail: Vul-RAG retrieves top-n knowledge-base entries (functional semantics, vulnerability causes, fixing solutions) via BM25 plus re-ranking keyed on LLM-extracted code semantics, then has the LLM sequentially reason over each retrieved item before a final verdict (Section 3, Figure 1).
threats_to_datum: Several evaluated models were released after PairVul's publication, so training-data contamination cannot be ruled out; output-format compliance issues bias results toward instruction-following models; the DeepSeek-Coder-V2 evaluation is incomplete due to GPU memory constraints (Section 6).

datasets: 450 NFT contract samples (custom, from real NFT projects / public vulnerability datasets)

key_numbers.metric: positive-label rate, slices+knowledge
positive-label rate, slices-knowledge
positive-label rate, complete contracts-knowledge

structure_gain: Slicing (vs complete contract, no knowledge) raises positive-label rate 73.78% -> 87.11% (+13.33pp); adding the ERC-721 knowledge base on top of slices raises it further to 97.11% (+10.0pp), with the same DeepSeek model/config held constant across all three arms (Section 5.4, Table 4).
confound_note: The three-arm ablation (slice+knowledge / slice-knowledge / full-contract-knowledge) holds the LLM (DeepSeek) fixed and cleanly varies representation and knowledge-injection, but the outcome metric is a raw 'positive label rate' with no independent ground truth, so the delta may partly reflect a shift toward over-flagging rather than true detection accuracy.
stop_detail: A structure-aware context-window algorithm regex-locates candidate statements, expands to a syntactically balanced function-scoped slice, and embeds an ERC-721-specific knowledge base plus a closed label set and explicit 'return None if insufficient evidence' rejection rule directly in the prompt (Section 4.2-4.3, Algorithm 1, Prompt 1).
threats_to_datum: Authors explicitly warn the positive-label rate 'must not be interpreted as classification accuracy' since there is no independently annotated ground truth, confusion matrix, or per-class precision/recall; model ID, temperature, and full knowledge-base content are unrecorded, limiting reproducibility (Section 6).
